sentences.text: The holotype individual of Hesperornithoides was estimated to be 89 cm long in 2019.
The Hesperornithoides specimen is considered to represent either an adult or a subadult individual.
The jugal bone of Hesperornithoides is pneumatic.
The third claw of the hand in Hesperornithoides is about the same size as the second claw.
The Hesperornithoides specimen preserves keratin sheaths on the tips of several toe and hand claws.
The generic name Hesperornithoides is derived from Greek words meaning "western bird form".
The specific name miessleri honors the Miessler family for their support of the research project.

A well-preserved skeleton of Hesperornithoides was unexpectedly discovered in 2001 by a team from the Tate Geological Museum in Jimbo Quarry, Wyoming, near the excavation site of Supersaurus vivianae.
The accidental discovery of the Hesperornithoides skeleton resulted in some fossils being damaged or lost.
The species Hesperornithoides miessleri was formally named and described in 2019 by Scott Hartman, Mickey Mortimer, William Wahl, Dean R. Lomax, Jessica Lippincott, and David M. Lovelace.
Hesperornithoides lived in a relatively open landscape with watercourses, few elevations, and few trees.
In 2019, Hesperornithoides was classified within the Troodontidae family in a relatively basal position alongside Daliansaurus, Xixiasaurus, and Sinusonasus.
Hesperornithoides belongs to the family Troodontidae.
In 2019, Hesperornithoides was placed in the family Troodontidae in a relatively basal position.
Unpublished phylogenetic analyses presented at the 2017 SVP conference determined that the specimen known as "Lori" was a relative of Sinovenator.

The presence of this advanced maniraptoran alongside other genera like Anchiornis and Eosinopteryx in Jurassic sediments refutes the argument of the "temporal paradox" used by those opposing the consensus that birds evolved from dinosaurs.
The parent group of Hesperornithoides is Troodontidae.
Hesperornithoides is classified under the class Reptilia.
The type species of the genus Hesperornithoides is Hesperornithoides miessleri.
Hesperornithoides miessleri lived approximately between 157 and 145 million years ago, during the Kimmeridgian and Tithonian stages of the Late Jurassic, in what is now North America.
Hesperornithoides lived from the Kimmeridgian to the Tithonian stages, between 154.8 and 143.1 million years ago.
There is one recorded fossil occurrence of Hesperornithoides in the Paleobiology Database.
